Fifteen comments

The Luck Penny

I got this tune from Clare concertina player, Dymphna O’Sullivan. I particularly like the F natural sequences in bars 3 and 4 of the third part of the tune which gives it a very distinctive flavour. In our local session we follow this with the two Pipe on the Hob jigs (both already posted on this site).

↳ Posted by Bannerman on January 15th, 2003.

The Luck Penny

On a historical note,the luck penny was (and maybe still is) an extra penny on the price agreed in horse fairs in Ireland.

↳ Posted by dafydd on February 28th, 2003.

Luck Penny, The

Try this as a 3rd part. It’s very similar to the Breathnach 3, No. 14 version, given as An Duthracht, which is the same tune, except for the little dip to bottom A towards the end.

(B/c/)|dBG GFG|dBG GAB | cA=F FEF | cA=F FBc|dBG GFG|gag fdB |def gdB |
cAF G2 B/c/ |dBG GFG |DGB DGB|cA=F FEF |C=FF A,FF |dBG GFG |gag fdB |de
f gdB |cAF G2||

I think it’s a much more attractive setting.

↳ Posted by Gerry_McCartney on March 4th, 2003.

The Luckpenny

Also to be found recorded on The London Lasses first album in a jig sandwich: Tenpenny Bit, The Luckpenny, Gallagher’s Frolics - track three - beautiful arrangement
